advances: Finite stopped process conditional on the specified transition and stopping matrices. Its inequality uses the modified terminal law.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The claim is vacuous if $I$ is empty. For each $i\in I$, apply the first-exit lemma to the positive transition weights and the original stopping atom of weight $D_{ii}$ at $p_i$. All row fibers have positive volume, the source residual is positive, and the displayed mean is precisely its barycenter. The lemma gives the new row weights, their mean, and a conditional expected residual root at most $f_i$. Boundary stops have residual root zero.

Set $B=C_0^{-1}D_{I,I}$. The row inequality is $Rf+Bf\le f$ on $I$. Since the new row has probability at least $\delta=\min_{i\in I}D_{ii}/c_i>0$ of stopping at an original site, $\lVert R\rVert_\infty\le1-\delta$. The nonnegative Neumann series converges and the process stops with probability one. The matrix $R^m B$ gives the probabilities of $m$ continuations followed by original-site stopping, so summing gives $W$. Iterating the row inequality yields $\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}R^m Bf\le f$ by nonnegativity, hence $Wf\le f$. The only other terminal events are the designated boundary contacts.
statement:
Let $C$ and $H$ satisfy the hypotheses of the first-exit correction lemma. At finitely many bases $p_i$ with positive-volume $d$-fibers, write $f_i=|C_{p_i}\cap H^c|^{1/d}$ and $I=\lbrace i:f_i>0\rbrace$. Assume a nonnegative transition matrix $T$ and a nonnegative diagonal stopping matrix $D$ with $T\mathbf 1+D\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1$, $\sum_jT_{ij}p_j+D_{ii}p_i=p_i$, and $D_{ii}>0$ for $i\in I$. For each $i\in I$, $j\notin I$ with $T_{ij}>0$, let $t_{ij}$ be the first exit fraction along $p_i$ to $p_j$, with exit point $b_{ij}$. Set $c_i=1+\sum_{j\notin I:T_{ij}>0}T_{ij}(1/t_{ij}-1)$ and $C_0=\operatorname{diag}(c_i:i\in I)$.

At $i\in I$ let a modified process continue to $j\in I$ with probability $T_{ij}/c_i$, stop at $p_i$ with probability $D_{ii}/c_i$, and stop at $b_{ij}$ with probability $T_{ij}/(c_it_{ij})$ on each exiting edge. Each modified row has mean $p_i$. With $R=C_0^{-1}T_{I,I}$, the probabilities of stopping by the $D$ rule at the original states in $I$ are $W=(\mathrm{Id}-R)^{-1}C_0^{-1}D_{I,I}$, and $W(f_i)_{i\in I}\le(f_i)_{i\in I}$ entrywise. The omitted row mass stops on contacts with zero residual volume.
title: Residual-root inequality for the finite first-exit stopped flow
